decisions.q: Who may withdraw a claim and who may mark delivery? docs/03 §4.7 only says EMPLOYEE_MANAGED cannot claim; nothing covers withdraw or deliver.
decisions.def: Follows the approved package steps. Withdraw: OWNER/MANAGER at any time, subject to state checks. Any other member only if they are the slot's claimedByUserId or assignedToUserId AND inside the 30-minute grace from claim_slots.created_at (any reason); otherwise 403 FORBIDDEN. Mark delivered: OWNER/MANAGER only; everyone else gets 403 FORBIDDEN. Uses the existing FORBIDDEN code, as claims.service assign() does.

decisions.q: PO confirmation needed: should EMPLOYEE_TRUSTED members (or the assigned person) also be allowed to (a) mark delivery and (b) withdraw after the 30-minute grace? The current default is no for both.
decisions.def: No for both (owner/manager only). The UI shows a short 'only owner or manager' note instead of the form.

decisions.q: When a project is cancelled after acceptance, are the winner's reserved credits refunded or consumed, per case (mutual, firm fault, client fault)?
decisions.def: No automatic rule. Only an admin can close the project (POST /admin/requests/:id/close) and must pick creditOutcome REFUND or CONSUME explicitly (no pre-selected option) plus a mandatory note. The close is audited and settled once through settleClaimSlot. The case records who reported and whether the other side confirmed, to inform the admin.

decisions.q: Should a mutual cancellation confirmed by both sides close the project automatically, without admin?
decisions.def: No. The confirmation is stored on request_project_cases.response=CONFIRMED_CANCEL and admins are notified; the admin closes it.

decisions.q: After how many days does a slot whose offer expired without a client decision get closed, and are its credits refunded or consumed?
decisions.def: Worker and sweep are implemented but gated by system_settings: expired_offer_autoclose_enabled=false, expired_offer_autoclose_days=14 (placeholder aligned with the 14-day validity/extension step of D-v6-7, used only if enabled), expired_offer_autoclose_credit_outcome=UNSET. The processor is a no-op unless enabled=true AND outcome is REFUND or CONSUME. Local verification flips them via PUT /admin/settings and restores them afterwards.

decisions.q: Does the 4.12 penalty 'Ofertă expirată / SLA ratat individual = 3 puncte' apply when a quote's validity lapses (or when it is auto-settled)?
decisions.def: No penalty is applied at quote expiry or auto-settle. The existing SLA-miss penalty stays as is.

decisions.q: How long before the offers expire should the client be reminded to decide?
decisions.def: No new lead time. The client gets a targeted quote.expired notification (bell and email) at the moment of expiry. It says the offer can no longer be accepted, offers 'Cere prelungirea', and states the auto-close date when auto-close is enabled. This comes before the settlement, which is what the package asks for.

decisions.q: Should the firm get an 'Am început execuția' action that sets IN_EXECUTION?
decisions.def: Not implemented; IN_EXECUTION remains a read-only accepted status as today.

decisions.q: Which final domain and which EU email provider (Brevo, Postmark EU or Amazon SES eu-central-1)?
decisions.def: Code stays provider- and domain-agnostic: everything goes through env (SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/SECURE, MAIL_FROM, SUPPORT_EMAIL, FRONTEND_ORIGIN, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL, gateway CANONICAL_HOST/LEGACY_HOSTS). No domain, provider hostname or address is hardcoded. docs/08 gets a cutover runbook the PO runs after choosing.

decisions.q: Which monitored mailbox is SUPPORT_EMAIL (e.g. suport@<domain>), and who reads it?
decisions.def: New SUPPORT_EMAIL env var. Required in production unless SMTP_ALLOW_DEV_HOST=true. Must be a valid email, not on a reserved/test domain, and not a no-reply/noreply/donotreply local part. When absent (dev), no Reply-To header and no support line are rendered.

decisions.q: Which emails carry Reply-To SUPPORT_EMAIL? Replies to chat or offer notifications could send private project content to the support inbox.
decisions.def: Opt-in per call (send(..., { replyToSupport: true })). Enabled for: email verification, password reset, account blocked, admin test email, and the notification events company.approved/rejected/suspended/unsuspended, payment.confirmed, subscription.expiring, withdrawal.decided, project.case_opened, project.cancelled. Not enabled for message.created, quote.*, claim.*, delivery.*, request.expired, project.delivery_reminder, project.overdue. The support footer line ('Ai nevoie de ajutor? Scrie-ne la ...') is shown on ALL emails when SUPPORT_EMAIL is set.

decisions.q: What goes in security.txt: a dedicated security@ contact, a Policy URL, and how long until Expires?
decisions.def: Contact: mailto:<NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL>. Expires = build time + 180 days (RFC 9116 asks for less than a year; every release rebuilds). Preferred-Languages: ro, en. Canonical: <SITE_URL>/.well-known/security.txt. No Policy line, because no disclosure-policy page exists yet (it is optional in RFC 9116). The route returns 404 when NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL is empty.

decisions.q: Where does the operator identity (legal name, CUI, J number, registered office) come from, given the PO has not sent it?
decisions.def: Reuse the existing admin-editable seller_* system settings (docs/03:202 'Date furnizor (seller) configurabile în Admin'; D-L0-1 'datele fiscale reale din Admin → Setari'). Add legal_contact_email ('') and a gate flag legal_identity_published ('false'). Show the identity only when the flag is 'true' and all five values are non-empty.

decisions.q: Exact legal entity data: legal name, CUI, J number, registered office, contact/DPO email. Is the operator the same entity as the invoice seller?
decisions.def: Blocked on the PO. After deploy, the PO sets seller_name, seller_cui, seller_reg_com, seller_address and legal_contact_email in Admin → Settings on the active slot, checks /ro/terms, then sets legal_identity_published=true.

decisions.q: Which Railway region hosts the production data services, and will the EU migration (eu-region-migration-plan, PROPUS) happen before launch?
decisions.def: Generic wording: hosting by Railway Corporation (USA). The application runs in the EU (Western Europe), and databases and file storage may be located outside the EEA. Transfers rely on the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (Art. 46(2)(c) GDPR) or, where applicable, the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework adequacy decision.

decisions.q: Which SMTP provider should the Privacy processor list name?
decisions.def: Name the provider if E-admin-platform-1's decision (Brevo / Postmark EU / Amazon SES) is recorded in docs/07 or CHANGELOG when this package is implemented. Otherwise use the category wording 'furnizorul nostru de trimitere a emailurilor tranzacționale' and flag it in CHANGELOG as a pending text edit that needs a version bump.

decisions.q: Legal review of the new Terms sections (delivery and auto-completion, reviews and disputes, penalties and suspension) and of the processor and transfer text, including Stripe's contracting entity and Railway's DPA/SCC status.
decisions.def: Implement drafts built strictly from docs facts: D-L1-1, 4.18, D-L1-3, 4.12 (company scope), D-L1-2 and invariant 3.8. The PO or a lawyer reviews them before the prod deploy.

decisions.q: Do admins also have to re-accept, and does privacy require 'acceptance' or only acknowledgement?
decisions.def: Admins are exempt. The dialog wording is 'I accept the Terms and acknowledge the Privacy Policy', and one click records both versions.

decisions.q: Should the backend block all API usage until the user re-accepts?
decisions.def: No. The block is in the UI only, through a blocking dialog on every [locale] route except /terms and /privacy, with Logout as the way out. The backend only computes the flag and records the acceptance.

decisions.q: Do purchased credite expire, and after how long? Can the rules page state credit validity?
decisions.def: Say nothing about credit validity on the page (no sentence either way). docs/03 4.16 says 'Creditele raman valabile 3 luni dupa expirarea abonamentului', but nothing in apps/backend enforces it, and the plan moves that decision to E-company-21 (Sprint 22). Disclosing an unenforced rule, or claiming credits never expire, would lock a policy either way.

decisions.q: Should the firm rules be a versioned legal document that forces re-acceptance (bump LEGAL_TERMS_VERSION or add a separate firm-rules version)?
decisions.def: No version bump and no new acceptance column. The Legal.terms text stays unchanged. The rules page says it details sections 6-7 of the Terms and shows the current Terms version label. The company register checkbox label links the rules next to the Terms. The link from the Terms page is a UI CTA below the article, outside the legal text.

decisions.q: Lawyer approval of the RO/EN text (done_when #1).
decisions.def: Ship the page ungated, like the Sprint 2 Terms, because it states only enforced rules with live values. Record 'revizuire juridica' as an open PO item in the CHANGELOG acceptance checklist (unchecked).

decisions.q: A suspended firm loses access to ongoing accepted projects (chat, fulfillment, quotes) because CompanyApprovedGuard blocks everything except /penalties. Is that the intended sanction?
decisions.def: Leave the behaviour untouched and describe it neutrally ('no access to firm work features during suspension'). Do not promise that ongoing projects continue.

decisions.q: Which e-Factura route: invoicing provider API (SmartBill/Oblio/FGO), direct ANAF SPV upload (UBL CIUS-RO + OAuth), or monthly accountant export/manual SPV upload?
decisions.def: Manual accountant route only, on provider-agnostic storage. Per-order e_invoice_status (PENDING/UPLOADED/VALIDATED/REJECTED/NOT_REQUIRED) plus anaf_upload_id/anaf_download_id. An audited admin PATCH records what the accountant did in SPV. There is a monthly CSV invoice register (GET /admin/billing/e-invoice-export?month=YYYY-MM) and an admin PDF download. No provider SDK, no UBL, no ANAF OAuth.

decisions.q: Invoices already issued with placeholder seller data (sellerSnapshot = seed values): storno or leave as is?
decisions.def: No code change. Those orders are backfilled to e_invoice_status=PENDING and show up in the export, so the accountant can decide. The storno flow stays post-MVP (payments.service.ts:361 comment, ro-invoice skill).

decisions.q: When STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_MODE=true is set on a production deployment (the rollout 'verify Checkout in test mode' window), should test payments still grant credits/subscription days?
decisions.def: Production refuses test keys at boot unless the flag is set. The flag is documented as 'isolated staging only'. When test mode is active, orders are created with test_mode=true: the benefit is granted, so staging flows work, but they NEVER get invoice_series/number and e_invoice_status is NOT_REQUIRED. Admin and wallet show a TEST MODE banner and the orders carry a 'Test' badge.

decisions.q: Which off-site EU provider and region should hold the backups (Cloudflare R2 with EU jurisdiction, Backblaze B2 eu-central, Hetzner Object Storage, Scaleway fr-par, AWS S3 eu-central-1)?
decisions.def: The code is provider-agnostic: any S3 endpoint through rclone, with OFFSITE_S3_PROVIDER/ENDPOINT/REGION/BUCKET/ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY set as env. Nothing is hard-coded. Local verification uses a second bucket on the dev MinIO. docs/08 lists the options and the 3 keys to create (write for daily, read for restore-test, read-only on the source for uploads).

decisions.q: Should production uploads stay on self-hosted MinIO (the official image pinned by digest, replacing bitnamilegacy) or move to a managed S3 (R2/B2/Railway buckets) during the EU migration? Decision 8 in docs/07 says 'Storage MinIO'.
decisions.def: Decision 8 (MinIO + S3 API + presigned URLs) stays as it is. This package adds a least-privilege policy, a service account, versioning and a 30-day ILM rule for the existing MinIO (setup-minio-uploads.sh). The EU plan lists both variants and marks 'official MinIO vs managed S3' as DECIZIE NECESARA. The app code only needs S3_* env values plus CORS if the store is managed.

decisions.q: What RTO target should be written in docs/08?
decisions.def: RPO = 24 h (follows from the approved daily schedule). RTO is written as 'tinta propusa 4 h, DECIZIE PO', and the monthly report shows the measured restore time so the PO decides with data.

decisions.q: Branch protection on main: branch protection and rulesets for PRIVATE repos need GitHub Pro/Team. Should we pay for it, or rely only on the CI gate before deploy?
decisions.def: The runbook requires tools/release/require-green-ci.mjs to pass (a green CI on the exact SHA) before any `railway up`. docs/08 gives the exact `gh api -X PUT .../branches/main/protection` command (required check 'verify', no force-push, no deletion) to run if the plan allows it.

decisions.q: Who receives the backup and restore-test report (BACKUP_REPORT_TO), and who holds the escrow of the keys (age identity, MESSAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, IP_HASH_SALT)?
decisions.def: BACKUP_REPORT_TO is a required env on both services. docs/08 recommends the real admin address and says it must be a monitored mailbox. For escrow, docs/08 lists the keys and requires 2 independent copies (password manager + an offline copy), with the holders filled in by the PO.

decisions.q: GDPR: encrypted backups keep data that users deleted in production for up to 12 months (monthly copies). Is this acceptable, and must the privacy policy mention it?
decisions.def: Keep the approved retention (30 daily + 12 monthly). docs/08 adds a rule: after any restore, re-apply deletions and anonymizations done after the backup date (from audit_logs). Legal text in ro/en.json stays unchanged.

decisions.q: Which dead-man switch should alert when the cron never runs (healthchecks.io, Better Stack, the error monitoring picked in E-admin-platform-8)?
decisions.def: Optional BACKUP_HEARTBEAT_URL, empty = off. On success the job does `curl -fsS -m 10 --retry 3 $URL`. On failure it always sends a FAILED email. A failed Railway cron is also visible in the dashboard.

decisions.q: Which error tracker do we use: Sentry EU (needs a DPA) or self-hosted GlitchTip?
decisions.def: A vendor-neutral Sentry-protocol integration, off by default. Backend: @sentry/node, active only when SENTRY_DSN is set. Frontend: @sentry/browser, active only when NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN is set, sending through a same-origin /monitoring tunnel. Scrubbing is strict, and no DSN is committed anywhere.

decisions.q: Which cookieless analytics do we use: Umami (self-hosted) or Plausible (EU cloud or self-hosted)?
decisions.def: lib/analytics.ts with two small adapters (umami: POST {host}/api/send; plausible: POST {host}/api/event). It is enabled only when NEXT_PUBLIC_ANALYTICS_PROVIDER, _HOST and _SITE_ID are set. It records only wizard_start and request_published, with fixed non-personal URLs, honours Do Not Track, sets no cookies and never throws.

decisions.q: Privacy page: under what name do we list the tracker and analytics processors?
decisions.def: Add two generic bullets to Legal.privacy.sections.sharing in RO and EN ('our error-monitoring provider (EU-hosted)' and 'our cookieless usage-statistics provider (EU-hosted)', each 'only when the integration is active'). This follows the existing unnamed email-provider bullet. LEGAL_PRIVACY_VERSION is not bumped.

decisions.q: How long are logs kept, and who can access them?
decisions.def: Document in docs/08 and security-close.md limit 1 that production logs live only in Railway and are kept for the Railway plan's retention (7 days on the current Hobby plan, to be confirmed in the Railway UI). Access is limited to Railway project members. Health probes are no longer logged, and LOG_LEVEL defaults to info. The Privacy retention text is left unchanged.

decisions.q: Which uptime-monitoring service, and who receives the alerts?
decisions.def: Document the monitor spec in docs/08: GET https://<public host>/api/v1/health/ready, alert on non-200 or on 'degraded' persisting for more than 5 minutes, check every 1 to 5 minutes, from an EU location. The implementer must not create accounts; the PO creates the monitor.

decisions.q: Should we build the admin ops panel (queue depth, outbox age) and an alert when the outbox is older than 2 minutes?
decisions.def: Not built in this package. It appears only in the PERF1-7 proposed fix, not in the approved steps, done_when or acceptance. Recommend a follow-up package.

decisions.q: Withdrawing an offer when the slot's assignee already holds another ACTIVE claim without an offer (partial unique index claim_slots_one_active_unoffered_per_assignee): refuse with 409, or unassign the slot?
decisions.def: Refuse with 409 ASSIGNED_USER_HAS_ACTIVE_CLAIM, checked under the lock before any write (the P2002 on that index is mapped to the same 409 as a backstop). Offer card message (RO): 'Nu poți retrage oferta acum: membrul atribuit are deja o altă preluare fără ofertă. Trimite oferta pe acea preluare sau atribuie-o altui coleg, apoi încearcă din nou.' Nothing changes in the database.

decisions.q: Should extend-validity after a long expiry extend from the previous validUntil or from now, and should withdrawing an offer after the slot's SLA deadline trigger an immediate SLA breach (hidden in R2-TESTS-6)?
decisions.def: Behaviour unchanged (newValidUntil = previous + days; withdraw re-adds the SLA job at the existing deadline). No test pins either behaviour.

decisions.q: Should a cerere stay claimable after its first oferta while claim slots (< max_claims_per_request) remain free (Option A, amend invariant 3.1), or does the first oferta close claims (Option B, state it in copy)?
decisions.def: Ship Option A behind system_settings key claims_open_after_first_offer = 'false'. Default behaviour stays exactly as invariant 3.1 (first offer closes claims). The public firm-rules page states whichever rule the flag produces. Do NOT edit docs/02 3.1 or docs/07. Record the open question in CHANGELOG under 'DECIZIE NECESARA'. When the PO decides A: the PO/implementer adds a docs/07 entry, amends 3.1 to read 'status in {IN_MARKETPLACE, CLAIMED_PARTIAL, OFFERS_RECEIVED, NEGOTIATION} and occupied < max_claims_per_request', and flips the flag in Admin → Setari.

decisions.q: If Option A is enabled, do late claimants get a protected window, i.e. should the client be blocked from accepting while a late claimant's SLA is still running?
decisions.def: Leave untouched. Each slot keeps its own SLA from claim time (docs/03 4.11, already implemented). The client may accept any offer at any time (ACCEPTABLE_REQUEST_STATUSES unchanged). A late claimant whose slot is still ACTIVE at accept is closed with a REFUND per D-L0-3, so it loses no credits.

decisions.q: Should landing/SEO copy ('Cel mult 3 oferte per cerere', 'primești până la 3 oferte comparabile') be rewritten?
decisions.def: No change. Both phrases are upper bounds that stay true under either rule. Only the firm-rules page gets the explicit rule sentence. If the PO keeps Option B permanently, marketing may still want to soften 'firmele concurează pentru tine'. That is a copy decision left to the PO.

decisions.q: Should firms mark each offer as priced with or without VAT and add advance/payment terms (two new quote_versions fields)?
decisions.def: Do NOT add fields or columns. VAT exists only on platform invoices (docs/03 4.17, D-L0 invoice decision); docs/04 has no such offer columns. In the accept dialog only, show a neutral text hint (Quotes.acceptConfirmVatHint) asking the client to confirm VAT and payment terms with the firm in the conversation. The hint can be removed once the PO decides.

decisions.q: docs/03 4.13 says the client 'poate accepta una din variantele existente'. Should the client be able to accept an OLDER version (for example v2 after the firm sent v3), not only the latest?
decisions.def: Only the latest version is acceptable (today's behaviour). Any other version id of the same quote returns 409 QUOTE_VERSION_CHANGED. The UI always shows and sends the latest version. accepted_version_id is stored, so allowing older variants later is only a rule change.

decisions.q: Should the client be blocked from accepting while their own change request is still PENDING (the finding notes that 'acceptable' ignores pendingChange)?
decisions.def: Leave the rule untouched: accepting the version the client sees stays allowed. The version check already guarantees they accept exactly what is on screen. A PENDING change request on an accepted quote stays harmless.

decisions.q: After a firm withdraws an offer, should the slot get a fresh re-quote window (e.g. sla_deadline_at = max(current, now + 1 working day)) instead of re-arming the original SLA deadline, which can expire the claim immediately (credits consumed + 3 SLA_MISS points)?
decisions.def: Keep the current rule (withdrawQuote re-arms the SLA breach job at the existing sla_deadline_at, L0-B). The dialog states the remaining time, or that the claim will expire immediately. If deadline + 12h grace has passed (and SLA is not paused), the server requires body {acknowledgeSlaBreach:true}, otherwise 409 QUOTE_WITHDRAW_SLA_ACK_REQUIRED with details.slaBreachAt and nothing written.

decisions.q: Can a firm cancel its own PENDING_ADMIN_REVIEW withdrawal?
decisions.def: Not implemented. The panel shows a clear 'Retragere în verificare la admin din {date}' banner, hides the withdraw form while a request is pending, and shows the admin note and decision date once decided.

decisions.q: For requests without an RON estimate (DESIGN_HELP, estimate 0), should the default bucket be 'Nu doresc să spun' instead of 'Sub 5.000 RON'?
decisions.def: Leave it unchanged: the stepped slider stays visible and keeps its current default (UNDER_5K), and the client can change it. Only requests that have an estimate are derived.

decisions.q: LIVE-20 / done_when: should every room with a 0 m length be rejected, including DESIGN_HELP (designBrief) rooms, which by the PO 2026-07-31 rule (CHANGELOG Z1, lines 925-926) publish without answers?
decisions.def: Reject zero or negative derived dimensions only where dimensions are required (strict mode: not ownProject, not designBrief) with CONFIGURATOR_ANSWERS_INVALID and details {roomIndex, stepId of the dimension-group, messageKey 'validation.dimensionOutOfRange'}; add a shared test that every registered dimension slot has min > 0. For own-project rooms (which now always come with a project file) and DESIGN_HELP rooms, treat zero as 'unknown' and show 'Dimensiuni nespecificate' instead of '0 × 0.6 × 2.6 m' in RoomSpecCard (firm and client views).

decisions.q: Wipe the Studio's local content (scenes and pieces in mm_studio_v3) on logout?
decisions.def: Keep the scenes and pieces (current behaviour). Clear only accountDraft {id,name}, which points to the previous user's server draft.

decisions.q: C4-4 proposed_fix: allow one 'Modifică și republică' edit while EXPIRED and a 'Duplică cererea' action once repost is used?
decisions.def: Not implemented. The EXPIRED + repostUsed state shows an explanation and a link to /requests/new ('Începe o cerere nouă'), as WF1-12 proposes.

decisions.q: What does 'stricter for admins' mean in practice? A lower threshold lets an attacker who already knows an email infer that it is an ADMIN account (lock after 5 attempts instead of 10).
decisions.def: LOGIN_MAX_FAILURES_ADMIN=5 in the same 15-minute window, with the same 15-minute cooldown, plus an audit row LOGIN_COOLDOWN_STARTED and an alert email on every lock. It is a single constant, so the PO can raise it to 10 to remove the role inference if preferred.

decisions.q: Which forwarded header carries the real client IP in production, and has the Railway edge been confirmed to overwrite it (the package's do_first)?
decisions.def: The code supports TRUSTED_CLIENT_IP_HEADER (expected x-real-ip). It is unset by default, which keeps today's req.ip behaviour. 'x-forwarded-for' is rejected by config validation. The header is honoured only when the socket peer is loopback. Production boot logs a warning while it is unset. The operator runs the spoof test (verify-slot's new spoof probe, or a curl with X-Real-IP: 203.0.113.77 against the public health URL comparing x-ratelimit-remaining) and then sets the variable on both app-blue and app-green.

decisions.q: Throttler in Redis adds about 150 ms per API request while Redis is still in another region. Accept that now, or keep in-memory storage on prod until the EU migration?
decisions.def: THROTTLER_STORE defaults to 'redis', with a 1000 ms command timeout and a per-process in-memory fallback on error or timeout. The PO or operator may set THROTTLER_STORE=memory on both slots until green-redis in EU West is live. The login lockout always uses Redis, since it only runs on login.

decisions.q: When should a firm see the client's contacts, and does revealing them affect the 30-minute free refund? Options: (a) contacts only after the 30-minute grace window; (b) contacts only after the firm's first chat message or offer; (c) keep reveal at claim but make the grace refund unavailable once contacts were seen; (d) cap grace refunds per firm per 30 days (what cap, and what happens above it?).
decisions.def: Keep W1 + I18 exactly as now. Add the setting claim_contact_reveal_policy with values 'ON_CLAIM' (default, today's behaviour) and 'AFTER_GRACE' (contacts and full address hidden until claim_slots.created_at + VOLUNTARY_WITHDRAWAL_GRACE_MS, FE shows when they appear). Admin can switch it from Admin > Settings with no deploy. (b), (c) and (d) are not built: (b) needs (c) to close the loophole, and (c) and (d) need a PO-defined consequence (consume? penalty?) that docs do not give. Log it as DECIZIE NECESARA in CHANGELOG and docs/04, not docs/07.

decisions.q: REQUEST_MODIFIED_POST_CLAIM: how long after the edit may a firm still withdraw with a refund?
decisions.def: Eligible only if last_edit_at > claim_slots.created_at AND no quote version of this slot (quote status not DRAFT) has sent_at > last_edit_at. The window closes when the firm sends an offer on the modified request. No hour limit is added. Ask the PO whether a fixed hour limit is also wanted.

decisions.q: Should the 48h auto-refund still be allowed after the firm has sent an offer (slot OFFER_SENT)? Pay-to-play consumes the credits of losing bidders.
decisions.def: Leave it unchanged. OFFER_SENT slots can still use CLIENT_UNRESPONSIVE_48H, but they now also need the firm-outreach condition.

decisions.q: How long after completion may non-managers still see a client's contacts (the 'warranty window')?
decisions.def: Add the setting completed_claim_contact_retention_days, default 0 = no cutoff (today's behaviour). When it is > 0, COMPLETED slots whose delivered_at (fallback: slot updated_at) is older than N days hide contacts from everyone except OWNER/MANAGER (reason RETENTION_EXPIRED). Admin validator: integer 0..3650.

decisions.q: The done_when asks for 'Decisions log shows the chosen contact and refund rule'.
decisions.def: Do not edit docs/07. Record the open question as DECIZIE NECESARA in CHANGELOG.md and in the docs/04 5.4 note next to the new setting. The PO writes the docs/07 entry once they decide; after that, only the setting value changes.

decisions.q: Should the public firm-rules page (Legal.firmRules) mention that government bridge days are also non-working days?
decisions.def: Leave the text unchanged. It already says working days exclude weekends and legal holidays. No Legal.* copy is edited in this package.

decisions.q: When a client types a phone, email or link in a description or free-text answer, block publishing or hide it from firms?
decisions.def: New system_settings key pre_claim_contact_text_policy, values MASK|BLOCK, default MASK (migration insert + seed + SETTING_DEFAULTS + admin validator + audit allowlist). MASK: publish succeeds, matches are replaced by ⟦contact⟧ in firm-facing DTOs, hits are logged. BLOCK: 400 REQUEST_CONTACT_INFO_IN_TEXT with per-field details, hits logged as BLOCKED. The client sees the inline hint in both modes.

decisions.q: Should admins be able to mark a detection as a false positive and unmask that text for firms?
decisions.def: Not implemented: the admin page is a read-only list (done_when only needs the list). If there are false positives, admins can switch the policy or ask for detector tuning.

decisions.q: Before a claim, should distance be shown only as bands (<5, 5-15, 15-30, 30+ km) instead of whole km?
decisions.def: New setting marketplace_distance_display = 'KM' (default): whole km computed from the snapped point (min 1). 'BAND' sets distanceKm=null and firms see only distanceBand. The DTO always includes distanceBand. There are no marketplace filters today, so filtering is unaffected.

decisions.q: What minimum coverage radius should a firm location have (the finding suggests 5 km; docs/07 D-v6-10 only sets the default of 50)?
decisions.def: Shared constant MIN_COVERAGE_RADIUS_KM = 2 (equal to the privacy grid cell; a smaller radius means nothing once points are snapped), enforced in the DTO and the zod schema on create/update only. Existing rows are not rewritten (local data is all 50/100 km).

decisions.q: How many locations can a firm have, and how often can it change them (the finding suggests a cap per plan plus a cooldown)?

Row-lock waits are not bounded by the claim profile's 10 s timeout (invariant 3.1). Measured live: POST /api/v1/claims blocked the full 24.6 s of a 25 s FOR UPDATE held in psql, and only then returned 503 DATABASE_BUSY (P2028). While it waits, the request holds a pool connection. Prisma's interactive timeout does not cancel the running query. There is no lock_timeout/statement_timeout anywhere in apps/backend, and apps/frontend/src/lib/api.ts has no fetch timeout. Result: a lock held longer than 10 s makes the user wait the whole lock duration, and the 'long lock -> DATABASE_BUSY copy' UI scenario ends in a late automatic success instead. A possible fix, which needs a decision: `SET LOCAL lock_timeout` equal to the profile timeout as the first statement in claim/critical transactions (one extra round-trip, about 150 ms cross-region), with SQLSTATE 55P03 (P2010) mapped to 503 DATABASE_BUSY in AllExceptionsFilter. Or set statement_timeout on the connection.
